speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) how can the various economic promotion agencies work closer together to support companies to grow and meet the challenges in this rapidly changing economic environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Over the years, the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore and International Enterprise (IE) Singapore have been the key economic agencies supporting Singapore companies' efforts to build up their capabilities and expand into international markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Both agencies also work closely with other Government agencies, such as the Economic Development Board (EDB), Info-comms Media Development Authority (IMDA) and Workforce Singapore (WSG), and this is to ensure that they meet companies' specific needs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In addition, we have 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) which bring together Government agencies and non-Government stakeholders, such as Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs), Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and training providers, to deliver integrated planning and implementation efforts to address the specific needs of each industry vertical.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But as we have all acknowledged, the economic environment is changing quite rapidly because of global digital connectivity, technological shifts and new business models.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: That, coupled with our tighter domestic constraints, means that external demand will be an even more important driver of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our companies must be able to respond nimbly to geopolitical and economic shifts, shorter technology cycles, and business model disruptions to tap on these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) has emphasised this and also the importance of the capacity to innovate, harness new technologies, scale up and internationalise, which are increasingly intertwined for all companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Hence, we have urged our companies and industries to transform themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And this is a message which must equally apply to Government agencies so that they adapt their programmes and, when necessary, restructure to better serve Singaporeans and our enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In arriving at this decision, we have also studied the feedback from various parties, including our TACs, as well as Members of Parliament (MPs) past and present, for a consolidated Government agency to champion the growth and development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Enterprise Singapore will integrate its knowledge of industries and its network of local and overseas partners to comprehensively support our enterprises, regardless of their size or stage of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Through Enterprise Singapore, startups will not only benefit from the capability development support that SPRING has been providing but also be plugged into IE's international networks.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SMEs will receive assistance to build their capabilities and seize opportunities in overseas markets to take their growth to the next level.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Large local enterprises can work with Enterprise Singapore to strengthen collaboration within their industry clusters and enhance the capabilities of the SMEs that support them.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In addition, Enterprise Singapore will deepen its partnerships with industry stakeholders, TACs, educational institutions and unions, to build strong local enterprises and create exciting new jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Enterprise Singapore and EDB will form two critical and complementary Government agencies that will help formulate and implement strategies for the development of industry clusters and enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Enterprise Singapore will also work closely with EDB to drive collaboration between multinational corporations, innovative startups and enterprises of all sizes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We believe that Enterprise Singapore will be well-positioned to build globally competitive local enterprises with deep capabilities and the ability to create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We look forward to working closely with all stakeholders to fulfil this important mission.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second question is: how would the new Enterprise Singapore develop the ethos and the culture that are in keeping with its mission to transform Singapore's economy?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And the merged entity would also need to regularly recruit people from the industry with experience to strengthen its business enabling capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that means no dilution or diminution in terms of the services rendered to the wide swathe of SMEs that we have in our ecosystem.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, that being the case, I fully expect that with the merger and creation of Enterprise Singapore, we will have a stronger hand in the way we are able to work with enterprises and through TACs to enable their growth and competitiveness to be strengthened.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The second point on the ethos and culture, that is an important point to be emphasised.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In any merger, that is one of the first questions that arises anyway because you are bringing in two organisations together.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You are trying to synthesis their missions and, as a result, there will always be questions about how one will prevail over the other, or will we be able to bring about a merger that actually results in one plus one being three, or more than two anyway.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As we bring them together, we think we can create a more durable economic model, complemented by what we have in terms of foreign investments.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In that capacity and in some of his earlier work, he has worked extensively with the business community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, he understands the requirements and so is also empathetic to the needs of the SME community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said all that, the next six months or so are going to be important.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There have been numerous exercises already in terms of town halls and engagements with senior management.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The senior officers will be deeply engaged, not only to bring the two organisations together, but to enhance their capacity to work with the industry going forward and to build a vibrant culture in the organisation as well.
